memory_update.text: Keep VRT as the reference benchmark for AI data-center thermal and power infrastructure, but do not let its high attention level crowd out smaller or less obvious thermal suppliers.

MOD is a high-priority Layer 2 candidate for the thermal-management node because its Airedale data-center cooling business has direct order and capacity-agreement evidence tied to AI/data-center customers.
AAON should be tracked as an underfollowed custom HVAC/liquid-cooling candidate; key verification is the size and repeatability of BASX/data-center cooling revenue.

NVT is a plausible underfollowed liquid-cooling ecosystem candidate because its AI/HPC exposure may sit in racks, enclosures, plumbing, power distribution, and cooling architecture rather than a simple HVAC label.

Need a follow-up pass for smaller micro/small-cap speculative shadows in pumps, valves, coolant, leak detection, thermal sensors, heat exchangers, and service/commissioning; evidence was not strong enough in this pass to include them over MOD, AAON, or NVT.
For the thermal-management node, keep JCI as a reference-scale chiller/controls anchor; it helps map the node but is too large and diversified for the underfollowed lane.

MOD, AAON, and NVT are the highest-priority underfollowed or semi-underfollowed US-listed candidates from this pass, but all now appear above or near the upper end of the preferred USD 300M-10B hunting range, suggesting the market may already be discovering the node.

The most testable thermal-management signals are data-center backlog, liquid-cooling revenue mix, named OEM/hyperscaler relationships, NVIDIA GB200/NVL72 architecture exposure, production-capacity constraints, and service attach rates.

Need an additional micro/small-cap shadow pass for narrower suppliers below the large-cap thermal names: pumps, valves, cold plates, heat exchangers, dielectric coolants, sensors, controls software, commissioning, leak detection, and maintenance/service contractors.

MOD should remain in the thermal-management universe due to explicit Airedale data-center cooling orders from a leading AI infrastructure developer and product exposure to free-cooling, controls, and CDUs.
AAON should remain in the thermal-management universe due to BASX-branded data-center cooling growth and Q1 2026 backlog strength tied to data-center demand.

NVT should remain in the thermal-management universe as a CDU/manifold/rack/PDU/service supplier, despite larger market cap, because its AI liquid-cooling exposure is direct and may be hidden inside electrical-connection classifications.

Thermal management should be tracked as a system chokepoint, not only a chiller category: evidence points to chillers, free cooling, CDUs, manifolds, rack infrastructure, controls, and field service as linked constraints.

This pass did not identify many clean USD 300M-10B US-listed pure plays with strong public evidence; smaller private or non-US suppliers may occupy key heat-exchanger, immersion-cooling, pump, valve, sensor, and service niches.
MOD should be promoted for deeper Layer 2 evidence work in the AI thermal-management node because Airedale has disclosed direct AI/data-center cooling orders and a large long-term capacity agreement.
AAON/BASX is a direct but execution-sensitive data-center liquid-cooling candidate; later layers should test production ramp, capacity, customer concentration, and margin conversion.
NVT is a component/platform candidate for CDUs, manifolds, racks, and power/cooling integration; evidence is product-level and needs revenue-materiality verification.

Thermal management is not just HVAC in AI data centers; the relevant chokepoint includes chillers, CDUs, manifolds, heat exchangers, liquid loops, controls, service, and customer-qualified reference architectures.

Next search pass should look for smaller US-listed component suppliers in heat exchangers, pumps, valves, sensors, refrigerants/coolants, maintenance services, and testing/commissioning firms, because this pass skewed toward already-publicized cooling-system vendors.

This pass keeps Vertiv as the reference leader and prioritizes Modine, AAON, and nVent as more underfollowed or less obviously labeled public-market mappings. No buy/sell recommendation is made.
